exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Press up and slightly back until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
tips: Keep a slight arch and your glutes on the bench.
Tuck your elbows to about 45–70° from your body.
Use a spotter or safety arms for heavy sets.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest
Elbows flared straight out to the sides

ranking.note: Total weight including the bar.

guide.overview: The classic upper-body strength lift. It trains the chest hardest, with the triceps and front shoulders helping, and lets you load more weight than most pressing movements.

Lie down with your eyes directly under the bar and plant your feet flat.
Pull your shoulder blades together and down, and keep a slight natural arch.

mistakes.what: Bouncing the bar off your chest
mistakes.why: The rebound does the work your chest should do and can bruise the sternum.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and touch lightly, or pause for a moment, before pressing.

mistakes.what: Elbows flared straight out to the sides
mistakes.why: A 90° flare puts the front of the shoulder in a weak, stressed position.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to roughly 45–70° from your torso as you lower.

mistakes.why: It turns the lift into a steep decline press and strains the lower back.
mistakes.fix: Drive through your feet into the floor but keep your glutes on the bench.

safety: Always use safety arms or a spotter for heavy sets, and never use a thumbless grip.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to 30–45° and lie back with the bar over your eyes.
Grip just wider than shoulder width with your shoulder blades pinned back.
Lower the bar to your upper chest just below the collarbones.
Press up until your arms lock out over your shoulders.
tips: A lower incline keeps more of the work on the chest.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

ranking.note: Total weight including the bar.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
